I’m writing this review with a broken heart. My mother-in-law is no longer with us, and I believe DR. SALMAN ALI SAYED (Nephrologist) at this hospital is responsible.
He misdiagnosed her condition - or failed to diagnose it properly at all. Her health deteriorated rapidly under his care. What could have been treated became fatal because of medical negligence.
We trusted this doctor with someone we loved. We believed he would help her. Instead, we lost her.
The rushed appointments, the failure to listen to our concerns, the lack of proper and unnecessary testing - it all added up to a tragedy that didn’t have to happen. This hospital treated her like a SOURCE of REVENUE, not a HUMAN BEING fighting for her life.
She’s gone now. Our family is shattered. And I have to live every day knowing that better care could have saved her.

To anyone reading this:

PLEASE get a second opinion. Ask questions. Demand answers. Don’t trust blindly like we did.

If this review saves even one person from what we went through, then maybe her death won’t be completely meaningless.

We will never get her back. Don’t let this happen to your family.

Is this really the level of professionalism expected from doctors at such a reputed hospital?
This entire experience was extremely disappointing. A hospital of this level should focus on basic respect, patient dignity, and proper communication. The staff and doctors seriously need training in behavior and patient handling.

महोदय/महोदया,

मैं, अपूर्व कुमार नौटियाल, आज 56 वर्ष की आयु में यह पत्र गहरी भावनाओं और कृतज्ञता के साथ लिख रहा हूँ। वर्ष 1971 से 1978 के बीच, जब मेरी आयु लगभग 2 से 5 वर्ष के बीच थी, मेरे बाएँ पैर में जांघ, घुटने के ऊपर तथा कमर के नीचे पतली टांग में दो महत्वपूर्ण आर्थोपेडिक ऑपरेशन आपके प्रतिष्ठित अस्पताल में सम्पन्न हुए।

मुझे सेरेब्रल पाल्सी है, और उस समय चिकित्सा सुविधाएँ आज की तरह आधुनिक नहीं थीं। फिर भी आपके समर्पित आर्थोपेडिक सर्जनों—विशेष रूप से डॉ. जेद्दा सर (यदि नाम स्मृति में त्रुटिपूर्ण हो तो क्षमाप्रार्थी हूँ) तथा डॉ. मोहिके सर—और उनकी टीम ने जिस कुशलता, संवेदनशीलता और देखभाल से मेरा उपचार किया, वह मेरे जीवन की आधारशिला बन गया।

भायखला तथा महालक्ष्मी में चले उस लंबे उपचार काल की स्मृतियाँ आज भी मेरे मन में सम्मान और कृतज्ञता से भरी हुई हैं। आपके अस्पताल की सेवा भावना और चिकित्सा समर्पण के कारण ही मैं आज समाज में सक्रिय भूमिका निभा पा रहा हूँ।

आज मैं दिव्यांग अधिकारों के लिए कार्यरत हूँ और अपने जैसे अन्य दिव्यांग जनों को जागरूक करने का प्रयास करता हूँ। यदि उस समय आपका उपचार और देखभाल न मिली होती, तो संभवतः मेरा जीवन मार्ग भिन्न होता।

भायखला रेलवे हॉस्पिटल, उसके डॉक्टरों, नर्सिंग स्टाफ और संपूर्ण टीम के प्रति मैं हृदय से आभार व्यक्त करता हूँ।

आप सभी को सादर नमन।

सादर,

To,
Medical Superintendent, Sir/Madam
Byculla Railway Hospital
Mumbai

Subject: Heartfelt gratitude for the life-saving treatment provided during the years 1971–1978

Sir/Madam,

I, Apoorva Kumar Nautiyal, am writing this letter today at the age of 56, with deep emotion and gratitude. Between 1971 and 1978, when I was approximately 2 to 5 years old, two important orthopedic operations were performed at your prestigious hospital on my left leg: the thigh, above the knee, and the narrow leg below the waist.

I have cerebral palsy, and at that time, medical facilities were not as modern as they are today. Nevertheless, the skill, sensitivity, and care with which your dedicated orthopedic surgeons—especially Dr. Jedda Sir (I apologize if I have any misprints) and Dr. Mohike Sir—and their team treated me became the foundation of my life.

The memories of that long treatment period at Byculla and Mahalaxmi still fill me with respect and gratitude. It is because of your hospital's spirit of service and medical dedication that I am able to play an active role in society today.

Today, I work for disability rights and strive to raise awareness among other people with disabilities like me. Had I not received your treatment and care at that time, my life path might have been different.

I express my heartfelt gratitude to Byculla Railway Hospital, its doctors, nursing staff, and entire team.

My respectful regards to all of you.

Sincerely,

💧 Drink clean, safe drinking water regularly throughout the day.

Maintaining healthy hydration habits, eating a balanced diet, and following good hygiene practices can help support your health during the monsoon season.

Monsoon season often brings an increase in fever-related illnesses, including dengue and viral fever. While both conditions may begin with a high temperature and body aches, they can have different causes and may require different medical evaluation.

Common signs of dengue may include:
• High fever
• Severe headache
• Pain behind the eyes
• Muscle and joint pain
• Skin rash

Common signs of viral fever may include:
• Fever with cough or sore throat
• Runny or blocked nose
• General body aches
• Fatigue

If your fever lasts more than two days, becomes very high, or is accompanied by persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding, severe weakness, or difficulty breathing, it is important to seek prompt medical attention.

Early assessment and appropriate care can help identify the underlying cause and guide suitable treatment. Staying hydrated, preventing mosquito bites, and maintaining good hygiene are important preventive measures during the monsoon season.

I have observed that the quality of service at the hospital has declined significantly compared to previous experiences. At the same time, the hospital charges have increased considerably, making the poor standard of service even more concerning.
I request the hospital management to investigate these issues seriously and take appropriate action to improve patient care, cleanliness, staff behavior, and room management policies so that patients and their families receive the quality of service they deserve.
